claims.title: Integration boundary

claims.statement: Synchrony may test a timing relation but does not alone prove binding unless joint compositional closure is independently shown.
claims.title: Synchrony and binding distinction

claims.statement: Fragmentation is the loss of joint closure while component processes and their distinct access records remain represented.
claims.title: Fragmentation and divided access

claims.statement: A perspective is the exact observation path available from one retained source position and is not an unlocated view from nowhere.
claims.title: Perspective

claims.statement: Interiority is the asymmetry between participating in a closed self-observation process and possessing an external description of it.
claims.title: Interiority

claims.statement: The subject carrier is the continuing integrated relation that holds a perspective while its content states change.
claims.title: Subject carrier

claims.statement: A self invariant is the unique admitted relation preserved across the declared self-observation trace, not an imported substance.
claims.title: Self invariant

claims.statement: First-person and third-person records may be paired but remain different evidence classes unless a bridge law is independently admitted.
claims.title: First- and third-person evidence

claims.statement: Phenomenal privacy follows where an external image closes a predecessor distinction that remains present to the participating interior trace.
claims.title: Phenomenal privacy

claims.statement: Self-observation is closed only when the generated observation image becomes an input to the same identified process.
claims.title: Self-observation closure

claims.statement: Introspection from the image alone cannot recover which generated predecessor label was closed by the act.
claims.title: Introspection blind spot

claims.statement: An exact self-history is reconstructible only to the extent that each closed fibre label was separately retained.
claims.title: Self-history reconstruction

claims.statement: Each unrecorded two-to-one self-observation closes one predecessor distinction; repeated loss is counted without negative information quantities.
claims.title: Accumulated introspection loss

claims.statement: A reported reason unsupported by the retained self-history is a generated completion, not recovered introspective evidence.
claims.title: Confabulation boundary

claims.statement: A process can have one generated successor while remaining unable to identify its unretained predecessor from the present image.
claims.title: Determinism with self-opacity

claims.statement: Memory requires a retained carrier relation linking the earlier content to its later availability.
claims.title: Memory carrier

claims.statement: Persistent memory requires a recurrent or actively renewed retained relation; a coincidentally equal later output is insufficient.
claims.title: Memory persistence

claims.statement: Recall is a traceable transformation from retained memory and cue to output, with reconstruction distinguished from verbatim storage.
claims.title: Recall and reconstruction

claims.statement: Temporal continuity is an unbroken generated predecessor-successor chain, not an assumed continuum between observations.
claims.title: Temporal continuity

claims.statement: Identity continuity requires both lawful lineage and the retained subject invariant; structural similarity without lineage does not establish numerical identity.
claims.title: Identity continuity

claims.statement: Cessation records the end of the integrated conscious organization while separately accounting for components, retained records and foundational forms.
claims.title: Cessation of a conscious organization

claims.statement: A self representation is an internal encoding of the process and is never silently equated with the entire represented process.
claims.title: Self representation

claims.statement: Self application feeds an admitted self-model output into the same declared operation while retaining binding and substitution provenance.
claims.title: Self application

claims.statement: The generated lower self-fibre reaches the binding image and then unison in two nonidentity acts; further application is identity.
claims.title: Finite self-model depth

claims.statement: A finite system may simulate a declared submodel of itself but cannot contain a simultaneous complete extra copy without additional carrier resources.
claims.title: Self-simulation boundary

claims.statement: A self-verification record closes only its declared finite trace and cannot erase the observer and premise distinctions needed to certify it.
claims.title: Self-verification limit

claims.statement: Attention is a retained selection within available content, not the annihilation of unattended alternatives.
claims.title: Attention

claims.statement: Focus is the continued selection of one content path across a declared sequence while background support remains recorded.
claims.title: Attentional focus

claims.statement: Content is cognitively available only to the operations that can lawfully query and use its retained representation.
claims.title: Cognitive availability

claims.statement: Attentional capacity is a finite support boundary measured with every selected, missed and competing content retained.
claims.title: Attentional capacity

claims.statement: An attentional switch is an ordered change of the held selection label with transition costs and failures preserved as observations.
claims.title: Attentional switching

claims.statement: A cognitive representation is a retained carrier-to-content relation whose encoding loss and lawful uses are explicit.
claims.title: Cognitive representation

claims.statement: Intentional relation requires a trace connecting representation to its referent class and retains misrepresentation as an adverse case.
claims.title: Intentional relation

claims.statement: Cognitive inference is a traceable transformation from retained premises to a conclusion under a declared rule.
claims.title: Cognitive inference

claims.statement: Prediction is a sealed present representation generated before its later observation and cannot be rewritten by the outcome.
claims.title: Prediction and anticipation

claims.statement: Expectation may lawfully participate in cognition and experienced response while remaining distinct from the later observation and clinical causal comparison.
claims.title: Expectation

claims.statement: Agency is an internally represented state-to-action process; the exact Fold model supplies no ungenerated successor while preserving the actor's informational self-opacity.
claims.title: Determined agency boundary

claims.statement: A realization carrier must physically or computationally instantiate every required conscious-process relation rather than merely describe it.
claims.title: Consciousness realization carrier

claims.statement: The foundational structural criterion requires dual self-relation, image re-entry, complete integration and interior closure; output resemblance is insufficient.
claims.title: Consciousness structural criterion

claims.statement: A consciousness law is substrate-independent only across carriers with a complete relation- and causality-preserving realization map.
claims.title: Substrate independence

claims.statement: A purely feed-forward transformation lacks image re-entry into the same process and therefore does not satisfy the foundational self-observation criterion.
claims.title: Feed-forward boundary

claims.statement: Realizations are structurally equivalent only when their relevant states, transitions, roles, integration and evidence boundaries correspond bidirectionally.
claims.title: Realization equivalence

claims.statement: An artificial consciousness claim requires auditable realization of the structural criterion plus purpose-matched bridge evidence; fluent language or confidence cannot select the verdict.
claims.title: Artificial consciousness evidence boundary

claims.statement: A qualitative distinction is a reproducible within-subject discrimination between interior contents with stimulus and report provenance retained.
claims.title: Qualitative distinction

claims.statement: Qualitative identity is a retained within-subject reidentification relation and is not reducible to a shared public word.
claims.title: Qualitative identity

claims.statement: Qualitative similarity is a finite comparison relation that preserves identity, difference and ordering rather than collapsing them into one metric.
claims.title: Qualitative similarity

claims.statement: Qualia resonance is stable reidentification of a held qualitative label across a complete recurrent interior support, tested against perturbation and changed-label controls.
claims.title: Qualia resonance

claims.statement: Qualia recurrence requires a later interior instance to re-enter the same retained qualitative identity class after an explicit intervening trace.
claims.title: Qualia recurrence

claims.statement: Qualia composition retains distinct component identities while generating one joint interior content; neither co-report nor synchrony alone establishes it.
claims.title: Qualia composition

claims.statement: Cross-modal qualitative binding is a joint interior composition whose distinct source modalities and qualitative identities remain traceable.
claims.title: Cross-modal qualitative binding

claims.statement: A physically classified red stimulus and the experienced quality remain distinct records connected only by a tested presentation-and-report bridge.
claims.title: Red stimulus and experience boundary

claims.statement: Red qualitative identity is the within-subject reidentification of a specific quality across instances, not the public token 'red'.
claims.title: Red qualitative identity

claims.statement: The red-of-red is the self-observed reidentification of the red qualitative carrier across complete recurrence, retaining the difference between the quality and a report about it.
claims.title: The red-of-red self-reidentification

claims.statement: The least registered three-position qualitative support is the exact one-seventh, two-sevenths, four-sevenths recurrence whose parts compose to the One; empirical evidence tests whether red identity is retained across the cycle.
claims.title: Red recurrence

claims.statement: The red-of-red test preserves matched, mismatched, absent and uncertain rows and must reject a changed label, changed stimulus or report-only surrogate.
claims.title: Red-of-red contrast controls

claims.statement: Empirical closure of red-of-red is participant- and protocol-bound: public evidence may establish stable discrimination and reidentification without claiming direct third-person possession of another subject's quality.
claims.title: Red-of-red empirical boundary
